With the rumors of Javale McGee and the Clippers, it looks like Doc might be turning to promising minimum contract big men, presumably because he's finding it hard to land a quality center in a sign-and-trade type deal. Here are some other guys in that vein who could maybe passably fill the gaping void at center:

Greg Smith

Smith only played 'major' minutes once -- in the 2012-2013 season with the Rockets -- when he broke into Houston's rotation as the team's primary backup center. The next year, Dwight Howard came in, which eliminated his role -- and he hasn't played since.

It's a little unfair, as Smith is actually decent. He's an excellent finisher inside (71.2 career FG% at the basket), has good hands, and is mobile. Asides from that, he has zero skills besides average offensive rebounding -- but alongside talented players he doesn't need anything else to be a really effective complementary weapon. Harden ran a mean spread pick-and-roll with Smith. Similar things could happen with him next to Chris Paul and Blake Griffin.

Jeff Withey

Withey's best known for blocking a ton shots, with good reason, as his 5.3% block percentage is pretty much elite. Of course, blocked shot numbers can be a bit misleading, but Withey is a genuinely good rim protector. Outside of that his defensive game isn't as strong, but that ability to stifle opponents' close-up shots is valuable.

And, on the other side of the floor, there's some promise: "Withy attacks the rim hard. He has a little Blake Griffin in him, meaning, he tries to dunk on people and forces them to either foul him or get put on a poster" (The Bird Writes). He doesn't finish at a high field goal percentage at the rim, but his career free throw rate of .637 is insanely good. Surely, CP3 and Blake could do something with that.

Ekpe Udoh

Udoh has always posted terrible box-scores stats, both traditional and advanced, but he's always been a (relative) plus/minus monster -- particularly on the defensive end. Udoh's an excellent team defender and rebounder, which is why his teams have always defended and rebounded better with him on the court despite his low steal, block, and rebound rates.

Greg Stiemsma

The Stiemer holds a special place in my heart for blocking six shots in his NBA debut -- which prompted Tommy Heinsohn to reasonably compare him to Bill Russell.

With that aside, Stiemsma is actually a really good rim protector. And he does enough elsewhere on defense that he meters out as a pretty good contributer on that end of the floor.

Of course, he takes back just about all his value on the offensive end of the floor, and he fouls at an astronomical rate when he's on the floor.

But, he's an okay finisher and has a decent long two, which might be just enough skill for, one more time, CP3 and Blake to make him not look incredibly godawful. And if you keep him in a 10-15 minute-a-night role his fouling can be kept in check.

Look, these aren't sexy options. But, if Clips get a couple of these guys, they could cobble together a rotation (with healthy doses of Blake at the five). And if one of them has a career year and center-Blake works out, things could work out for them. Of course, it'd be untenable, especially in the playoffs, but that's not to big of an issue as this season the Clippers are merely going to be treading water, waiting for the free agency bonanza of 2016.
